blockNote: Hit knockback and recovery controller (Bank 00, 55415-55927). One short-lived actor is spawned per hit. It slides the victim along one axis for 16 frames by moving ITSELF (collision-checked movement) and copying its position to the victim every frame, then either hands control back (player) or resolves the hit (enemy: HP check, hit / death callback). It has no sprite and is never placed by a scene.
=== SPAWN CONTRACT ===

Four spawn sites: ApplyPlayerHitstun and combat_collision.ApplyInteractionDamage (flags word $2400, victim = the player) and the two enemy-hit paths in combat_collision (flags $2000). The flags word becomes the child's $10: $2000 = script-driven run path (own wait counter; actor_execution moves such an actor only while $12 bit 3 is set), $0400 = 'the victim is the player': the controller tests it to choose HitStaggerReturnAI instead of HitStaggerResolveHit (the old note said $0400 marks an enemy and that ReturnAI 're-enables AI for enemies'; ReturnAI only ever handles the player). CopyActorState gives the child the victim's position, anim index, $12 (without $1000) and, in $24, the victim's slot. The spawner then stores a direction code in the child's $28 and zeroes its $2C / $2E, and copies the victim's extendedFlags bit $0020 ('hitstun skip' in the WRAM map) into the child.

Direction code in $28: 0 = south, 1 = north, 2 = west, 3 = east (CalcKnockbackDirection), 4 or more = no knockback. free101C ($7F101C) of the victim is a knockback TIER: 0 for ordinary actors, 1 for the player (player_character init) and mu5F_cyclops; the only writers in extracted/ are CopyActorState (zero), those three and this file (copy to the child).
=== HitStaggerMain ===

$10 |= $0008 (collision-checked movement) unless the victim has extendedFlags $0020; $12 |= $0008 (movement request for a script-driven actor). If $12 bit $0010 is set (inherited from the victim: stagger-immune in combat_collision) or the direction code is 4 or more, there is no knockback: WaitByte #$0F (16 ticks), then ReturnAI (player) or ResolveHit. Otherwise the victim's pixel X / Y are saved in orbitAngle / orbitDiameter ($7F0010 / $7F0012: no orbit here, the words are reused as the START position), the tier is copied, and the direction code is decoded by chained DEC / BMI (the old note spoke of a '3-deep stack-encoded direction index'; there is no such stack): 0 = Y chain (carry set), 1 = Y chain with ForceDirBoth (negated), 2 = X chain with ForceDirBoth, 3 = X chain (carry clear). Each branch first clears the inherited ForceDir bits ($6000 of $12). The branches JSR HitStaggerApplyKnockbackDelta, which pushes HitStaggerStoreMovementDelta as a return address; that routine stores the movement chain head in $2E (carry set, $26 := 0, vertical) or $2C (carry clear, $26 := 1, horizontal; the old doc had the axis flag the other way round). The RTS chain ends in HitStaggerDirection (pushed by Main).

Curves (movement_delta_table, one delta per frame, pixels): tier 0 uses entry $22 = 4 4 5 5 5 5 4 4 3 3 2 2 1 1 0 (sum 48 px = 3 tiles); tier 1 and above use entry $23 = 3 3 4 4 3 3 2 2 2 2 1 1 1 1 0 (sum 32 px = 2 tiles). The player is tier 1.
=== HitStaggerDirection (the 16-frame slide loop) ===

SetEntryHereAndYield, then LoopStart #$10: 16 frames in which the child's $14 / $16 are copied into the victim. After the loop: the player ($10 bit $0400) goes to ReturnAI. An enemy without $10 bit $0008 goes straight to ResolveHit. Otherwise the distance travelled along the axis ($26 = 0: Y, else X) is d = |start - current|: d = 0 resolves at once; if d is a multiple of 16 HitStaggerCheckKnockbackDistance compares it with the tier threshold (tier 0 $30, tier 1 $20, tier 2 and above $40) and carry CLEAR (equal = the full slide happened) resolves; any other d is a CUT-SHORT slide (a wall stopped it): the victim's chain pointer and delta word on the knocked axis are zeroed ($2E and $7F002E for a vertical slide, $2C and $7F002C for a horizontal one) and its wait counter $08 is zeroed when it has no chain on the other axis, so its script resumes immediately (purpose inferred, OQ-I046-3). The thresholds equal the curve sums (48 and 32), which is why a full slide matches exactly; tiers 2 and 3 use the 32-px curve with a $40 threshold and could never match (no actor uses them).
=== HitStaggerResolveHit (enemy) ===

HP ($7F0026) nonzero: if onHitCallback ($7F1000) is set it becomes the victim's entry address (low word only, the bank word is unchanged) and is cleared; the victim's iframe counter becomes $FFF4 (-12, recovery). HP zero: the victim's $10 gets $0040 (dead) unless it already has it, its entry becomes onDeathCallback / onDeathCallbackBank when set (and $08, $2C, $2E are zeroed) or StandardEnemyDefeatHandler in the same bank. Finally X := D (the child) and COP Die, because the COP needs X = the actor slot.
=== HitStaggerReturnAI (player only) ===

Unless playerFlags has $0A00 (game over / script lock) the player's entry address becomes player_character.PlayerIdleEntry. The player's iframe counter is set to $FFE2 (-30) and the D-pad bits $0F00 of joypadMaskStd are cleared (shown again). Because a positive counter freezes the player controller, overwriting the $003C that ApplyPlayerHitstun wrote ends the stun after the 16-frame slide (about 17 ticks), not after 60; a heavy hit's -60 is likewise shortened to -30.
=== Helpers ===

HitStaggerCheckKnockbackDistance stores d in the absolute scratch $0000 and pushes HitStaggerKnockbackCallbackPass - 1, so the CMP's RTS lands in CallbackPass, which turns Z into carry (CLC when equal, SEC otherwise). All operands written with four hex digits ($0000, $002C, $002E, $0008 ...) are absolute addresses; $0000 is the global scratch word, the others are the slot fields indexed by X.
Everything here is UNVERIFIED-RUNTIME (no emulator trace); the arithmetic and flow are read from the code and the movement_delta_table nodes.

HitStaggerMain: Entry of the child. Sets the movement flags, saves the victim's start position and tier, decodes the direction code (0 S, 1 N, 2 W, 3 E; 4+ or a stagger-immune victim = no knockback) and chains into the slide loop.

HitStaggerApplyKnockbackDelta: Pushes HitStaggerStoreMovementDelta as the next return address and selects the table offset by tier: $44 (entry $22, 48 px curve) for tier 0, $46 (entry $23, 32 px curve) for every other tier. Carry (from the caller) is preserved for the store.
HitStaggerStoreMovementDelta: Reads the chain head from movement_delta_table + Y. Carry set: Y chain in $2E and $26 := 0 (vertical). Carry clear: X chain in $2C and $26 := 1 (horizontal).
loc_00DA73: Vertical: store the chain head in $2E and clear the axis flag $26.

blockNote: Player damage and knockback entry (Bank 00, 50071-50198), called by JSL from enemy attack scripts. Registers: A = damage with bit 15 as a 'heavy hit' flag, Y = knockback direction code (0 south, 1 north, 2 west, 3 east, 4 or more = none). The old header said 'damage in Y and knockback metadata on the stack' and that damage is halved; neither is true.
=== STEPS ===

1. $0000 := Y (absolute scratch, kept for later) and $0002 := 0. ASL moves bit 15 of A into carry: when set, $0002 := $FFC4 (the heavy-hit counter). LSR restores the damage with bit 15 cleared; it is NOT halved (ASL then LSR cancel out).
2. playerHp := max(0, playerHp - damage). D and X become the player actor.

3. Player flags $10 |= $0080 (hit reaction); the iframe counter ($7F0028) := $0002 if nonzero, else $003C. A positive counter is hit-stun, a negative one is recovery / invincibility (see actor_execution).

4. If playerFlags bit $0800 (script / ability lock) is set, no stagger is spawned: only the D-pad bits $0F00 of joypadMaskStd are cleared. Otherwise HitStaggerMain is spawned with COP SpawnListAppend ( entry, 0, 0, #$2400 ): $2400 is the child's FLAGS word ($2000 script-driven, $0400 player victim), not a priority as the old header says. Y = the child slot afterwards.

5. Y = $1FC0 means the actor pool was full and the spawn failed: the D-pad bits $0F00 are cleared (some callers hide them first; the child that would have restored them does not exist). The code still falls through to the child-setup stores below with Y = $1FC0, unlike ApplyInteractionDamage, which skips them (OQ-I046-2).

6. Child setup: extendedFlags bit $0020 of the player is copied to the child, the direction code from $0000 goes into the child's $28, and its $2C / $2E are zeroed. Hit sound: PlaySoundCh2 #07 (always the Will sound; combat_collision picks #08 for Freedan and Shadow).

The function never HIDES the D-pad (the old header said it masks joypad input 'for heavy hits or when the climbing flag is active'): it only reveals it on the two no-stagger paths. Callers such as gw82_archer and ir1F_stone_guard hide it themselves (TSB #$0F00) before the JSL, and HitStaggerReturnAI reveals it when the stagger ends.
Because HitStaggerReturnAI overwrites the iframe counter with $FFE2 when the slide ends, the $003C written here only lasts until then (about 17 ticks).
=== CALL SITES (9, in 3 files) ===
| File | A | Y |
| gw82_archer (2 sites) | 2, 2 | 3 (east), 2 (west) |
| gw83_asp (3 sites) | 1, 1, $8001 (heavy) | 4, 4, 4 (no knockback) |

$0B02 is the difficulty level (ram_map.txt), so the stone guard's two strongest hits add it to a base of 2. The old docs say about 12 callers; there are 9. Combat hits from the player's own attacks and from contact use combat_collision's inline code instead.
Everything here is UNVERIFIED-RUNTIME (no emulator trace); read from the code.

blockNote: Enemy defeat dispatcher with a kill counter (Bank 0A, 697407-697568). A trimmed variant of StandardEnemyDefeatHandler used as a death callback by three enemies: gw82_fire_bug (SetDeathCallback code_0B8DB9), av6D_dive_bat (code_0AEF2E) and gw8A_sand_fanger (JumpFar), each reaching it with COP JumpFar. $0AEC is the number of enemies left on the map (hex) and $0AEE the same count in BCD (ram_map.txt).
=== FLOW ===

- $0AEC = 1 (this is the last enemy): clear the ForceDir bits ($6000 of $12), halt movement (StageMoveXY #0, #0 selects the zero chain; moveScratch1 / 2 = $7F002C / $7F002E cleared) and JumpFar into StandardEnemyDefeatHandler, which decrements the counters itself, plays the full defeat and gives the clear reward (EnemyStatBonusReward when the remaining count reaches 0).

- Otherwise: CallNear code_0AA474 (below), then SpawnAfterFlags ( @field_reveal_object, #$0020 ), store the remaining count (orbitAngle, saved by the subroutine) in the child's $26 and Die. field_reveal_object treats a nonzero $26 as 'use this enemy's own stats': FieldRevealFromActorStats reads the low two bits of the stat-table byte at +3 (0 none, 1-3 a HP / STR / DEF gem) of the defeated enemy, so every kill but the last can drop its own stat gem (the old note: 'Spawn stat gem reveal').

code_0AA474 (a CallNear subroutine, returns with RestoreSavedPtr): death sound #03 (the standard handler uses #06), BCD decrement of $0AEE, hex decrement of $0AEC stored also in orbitAngle ($7F0010,X) for the spawned actors, halt movement, spawn EnemyDeathFlash (flags $0302), SetDungeonKillFlag (the actor's enemyNum bit in the wramFlags bitfield), $10 |= $2000 (script-driven run path), ClearSolidHere when extendedFlags bit $0008 is set, and the field-reveal bookkeeping: when deathActionIdx ($7F0024) is nonzero and event flag $0100 + idx is not yet set (TestFlag_0100 carry clear), set it and spawn SpawnFieldRevealEffect (flags $0342) with the index copied into the child's deathActionIdx.

Differences from StandardEnemyDefeatHandler: no boss / stat-table checks (the three callers are ordinary enemies), no WaitByte, no EnemyGemDropRouter call (a field_reveal_object child is spawned instead; it reads the same stat-table byte at +3), and the $12 |= $1000 priority boost on the flash is not applied. The old header said it 'decrements ... plays death SFX, spawns death flash, sets dungeon kill flag, optionally clears collision tile' which is right; it did not explain the field_reveal_object spawn or the callers.
Edge case: the test is for exactly 1. If $0AEC were 0 the counters would wrap to $FFFF / $99 (BCD) and $26 would be nonzero (OQ-I046-4). UNVERIFIED-RUNTIME.

EnemyDefeatDispatch: Entry (X = defeated actor). Last enemy ($0AEC = 1): halt and JumpFar to StandardEnemyDefeatHandler. Otherwise run code_0AA474, spawn field_reveal_object with the remaining count in $26, and Die.

loc_0AA4B8: Field-reveal bookkeeping: skip when deathActionIdx is 0 or its $0100-base event flag is already set; otherwise set it and spawn SpawnFieldRevealEffect with the index.
loc_0AA4E0: Return to the caller of the CallNear subroutine.
